insulins.overview: A mealtime (bolus) insulin with a faster onset than standard rapid-acting aspart, according to its US label's pharmacodynamic study.

onset.display: About 16–20 minutes to first measurable effect (dose-dependent in the label study)

peak.display: About 91–133 minutes (dose-dependent in the label study)

duration.display: About 5–7 hours for effect to return to baseline (dose-dependent in the label study)

routes.display: Subcutaneous injection, and intravenous infusion only under medical supervision (label §2.2)

pumpCompatibility.display: Use with an insulin pump depends on the pump manual; PumpCart is listed (label §2.2)

storage.display: Unopened vials refrigerated 2–8°C. Unopened pens and PenFill: 28 days at room temperature or refrigerated until expiry. In-use vial and pen: 28 days. PumpCart has its own limits. Check the full table in the label.

mixing.display: Do not mix with any other insulin (label §2.1). Do not draw into a syringe for later use (§16.2).

formulationDifferences.display: Same active ingredient as the standard rapid-acting aspart product, with a different formulation. Do not treat as interchangeable without clinician guidance.

safetyNotes: Hypoglycaemia is the most common risk with any insulin.
Do not mix with other insulins (label §2.1).

insulins.overview: A mealtime (bolus) insulin with a faster onset than standard rapid-acting lispro, according to its US label's pharmacodynamic study.

onset.display: About 15–17 minutes to first measurable effect (7–30 units in the label study)

peak.display: About 120–174 minutes (7–30 units in the label study)

duration.display: About 4.6–7.3 hours for effect to return to baseline (7–30 units in the label study)

routes.display: Subcutaneous injection at the start of a meal, or within 20 minutes after starting; intravenous use for U-100 only under medical supervision (label §2.2)

pumpCompatibility.display: U-100 only. Refer to the pump manual to confirm compatibility (label §2.2).

storage.display: Refrigerate unopened pens, cartridges and vials at 2–8°C until use. Unopened at room temperature: 28 days total. In-use pens and cartridges: 28 days at room temperature, do not refrigerate. In-use vials: 28 days.

mixing.display: Do not mix with any other insulin products (label §2.1). Do not dilute or mix U-100 when using a pump (§2.2).

formulationDifferences.display: Different concentration and formulation from U-200 presentation. See the separate U-200 record.

safetyNotes: Hypoglycaemia is the most common risk with any insulin.
Do not mix with other insulins (label §2.1).

insulins.overview: The U-200 presentation of Lyumjev. Its pharmacodynamic values are not yet recorded in this explorer, so they are shown as pending review.

pumpCompatibility.display: Not for use with a continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion pump (label §2.1)

storage.display: Same refrigeration and in-use rules as U-100 pens (label §16.2). Check the table for U-200.

mixing.display: Do not mix with any other insulin (label §2.1).

formulationDifferences.display: Twice the concentration of the U-100 product. Do not treat as interchangeable with U-100 without clinician guidance.

safetyNotes: Concentration differs from U-100. Confusing the two can cause dosing errors.

insulins.overview: Standard rapid-acting mealtime insulin. Pending review: clinical values are not yet source-checked here.
A rapid-acting mealtime insulin. Its US label describes a faster onset and shorter duration than regular human insulin.

onset.display: Not given as a number of hours in the label text reviewed. The label describes faster onset than regular human insulin (§12.2).

peak.display: Peak serum levels 30–90 minutes after dosing (healthy volunteers, subcutaneous, 0.1–0.4 unit/kg; §12.3)

routes.display: Subcutaneous injection, continuous subcutaneous infusion (pump), and intravenous infusion (§2.2)

pumpCompatibility.display: U-100 is approved for continuous subcutaneous infusion using an insulin pump (§2.2)

storage.display: Unopened refrigerated: until expiry. Unopened at room temperature: 28 days. In-use pens and cartridges: 28 days at room temperature, do not refrigerate. In-use vials: 28 days.

mixing.display: May be mixed with NPH insulin only (§2.5). Do not mix with any other insulin in a pump (§2.2).

formulationDifferences.display: Same ingredient as the U-200 product, at half the concentration. Do not treat the two as interchangeable.

safetyNotes: Mixing rules are specific: NPH only, and not in a pump (label §2.2, §2.5).
Hypoglycaemia is the most common risk with any insulin.

insulins.overview: The U-200 presentation of Humalog. Its pharmacodynamic values are not yet recorded here, so they are shown as pending review.

pumpCompatibility.display: Not for continuous subcutaneous infusion by pump (§2.2)

storage.display: Same refrigeration and in-use rules as the label's table for U-200 pens (§16.2).

mixing.display: Do not mix with any other insulin (§2.5).

formulationDifferences.display: Twice the concentration of U-100 Humalog. Do not treat as interchangeable with U-100.

safetyNotes: Concentration differs from U-100. Confusing the two can cause dosing errors.

insulins.overview: Rapid-acting mealtime insulin. Pending review: clinical values are not yet source-checked here.
Short-acting human insulin. Pending review: clinical values are not yet source-checked here. Regional brands are listed in the market section once verified.
Intermediate-acting human insulin. Pending review: clinical values are not yet source-checked here.
A long-acting basal insulin. Its US label describes no pronounced peak. Biosimilar and follow-on products are not yet recorded here.

peak.display: No pronounced peak, compared with NPH insulin (§12.3)

duration.display: About 24 hours; range 10.8 to more than 24 hours, to end of pharmacological effect (§12.2)

routes.display: Subcutaneous only. Do not administer intravenously or via an insulin pump (§2.1).

storage.display: Unused: refrigerate 2–8°C. Unopened at room temperature: 28 days. In-use vial: 28 days, refrigerated or room temperature. In-use pen: 28 days at room temperature only, do not refrigerate.

mixing.display: Do not dilute or mix with any other insulin or solution (§2.1).

formulationDifferences.display: Different from the U-300 product (Toujeo) in concentration and profile. Do not treat as interchangeable.

safetyNotes: Hypoglycaemia is the most common risk with any insulin.

insulins.overview: A long-acting basal insulin. Pending review: clinical values and current regional availability are not verified here.
An ultra-long-acting basal insulin. Its US label reports glucose-lowering effect over a steady-state dosing period, and no glucose-lowering onset time.

onset.display: Not stated as a glucose-lowering onset. Insulin degludec reached plasma at a median of about 1 hour (§12.3).

peak.display: Glucose-lowering peak (GIRmax) at a median of about 12 hours, steady state (§12.2)

duration.display: At least 42 hours after the last of 8 once-daily doses (steady state; §12.2)

routes.display: Subcutaneous, into the thigh, upper arm or abdomen (§2.1)

pumpCompatibility.display: Not for intravenous use or in an insulin infusion pump (§2.1)

storage.display: Unused: refrigerate 2–8°C until expiry. In use: 56 days, at room temperature up to 30°C or refrigerated (label Table 18).

mixing.display: Do not dilute or mix with any other insulin or solution (§2.1).

formulationDifferences.display: Different concentration and duration profile from U-200 Tresiba. Do not treat the two as interchangeable.

safetyNotes: Hypoglycaemia is the most common risk with any insulin.

insulins.overview: The U-200 presentation of Tresiba. Its pharmacodynamic values are not yet recorded here, so they are shown as pending review.

routes.display: Subcutaneous, into the thigh, upper arm or abdomen (§2.1)

pumpCompatibility.display: Not for intravenous use or in an insulin infusion pump (§2.1)

storage.display: Same refrigeration and in-use rules as the label's table for U-200 pens (Table 18).

mixing.display: Do not dilute or mix with any other insulin or solution (§2.1).

formulationDifferences.display: Twice the concentration of U-100 Tresiba. Do not treat as interchangeable.

safetyNotes: Concentration differs from U-100. Confusing the two can cause dosing errors.

insulins.overview: A U-300 long-acting basal insulin. Its US label gives onset and peak information, but does not state a duration of action.
presentations: 3 mL Max SoloStar prefilled pen (900 units)

onset.display: Develops over about 6 hours after the dose (§12.2)

peak.display: Median time to maximum serum insulin concentration 12–16 hours (§12.3)

duration.display: Not stated as a duration of action in the label. Serum insulin reached the lower limit of quantitation by 16–36+ hours (§12.3).

routes.display: Subcutaneous, into the abdomen, thigh or deltoid (§2.1)

pumpCompatibility.display: Not for intravenous use or in an insulin pump (§2.1)

storage.display: Unused: refrigerate 2–8°C until expiry. In use: room temperature up to 30°C, do not refrigerate. In-use expiry 56 days.

mixing.display: Do not dilute or mix with any other insulin products or solutions (§2.1).

formulationDifferences.display: 300 units/mL, which is three times the concentration of U-100 glargine. Do not treat as interchangeable with U-100 products.

safetyNotes: Concentration differs from U-100 glargine. Confusing the two can cause dosing errors.

insulins.overview: A premixed product: a fixed mixture of rapid-acting and intermediate-acting insulin in one vial or pen. It is not a basal or bolus product on its own. Pending review.
A premixed human insulin: regular and NPH insulin mixed in a fixed ratio. Pending review. Regional brand availability is not yet verified.
A premixed lispro insulin. Pending review: clinical values and regional availability are not yet verified here.
A co-formulation of a basal component (degludec) and a bolus component (aspart) in one pen. It is not the same as a premixed product such as biphasic insulin aspart 30. Pending review.
